records.statement: Pass identity: def MarkStrideAlign : Pass<"hivm-mark-stride-align", "func::FuncOp">, summary 'Automatically annotate stride_align marks for operands of hivm ops', description 'For all hivm ops, annotate their memref operands with storage_align marks automatically', constructor mlir::hivm::createMarkStrideAlignPass(), dependentDialects memref/hivm/annotation (Passes.td:876-886); DEBUG_TYPE 'hivm-mark-stride-align' and MarkStrideAlignPass : impl::MarkStrideAlignBase (MarkStrideAlign.cpp:32, 52-56, 1116-1118).

The mark itself: shared helper createAlignMarkOp (declared in Util.h:111-116 with default attr names hivm::StrideAlignDimsAttr::name and hivm::StrideAlignValueInByteAttr::name) creates an annotation::MarkOp inserted immediately after the marked value and sets two dense-i32-array attributes on it, stride_align_dims and stride_align_value_in_byte; empty alignDims produces no mark (PropagateAlignUtil.cpp:1777-1790). The attributes are defined in HIVMAttrs.td: HIVM_StrideAlignValueAttr StrideAlignDims = stride_align_dims (:1265-1269), HIVM_StrideAlignValueInByteAttr = stride_align_value_in_byte (:1271-1276), and HIVM_SkipStrideAlignForVLoadAttr = skip_stride_align_for_vload, documented as marking an alloc whose downstream vload-d buffers must skip stride alignment because the resulting inter-row gaps would break vldsx1 (128-element consecutive flat-pointer load) (:1278-1285).

markAlignedDim legality and value: no alignDim -> no mark; TensorType operand -> emitError 'Not bufferized.'; unranked MemRef -> 'UnrankedMemRef not supported.'; layout neither identity nor StridedLayoutAttr -> 'Non-strided-memref not supported.'; alignDim > rank-1 -> 'align dim is too large.'; otherwise it calls createAlignMarkOp with {alignedDim} and {getHWAlignBytes(memrefTy.getMemorySpace())} as the align bytes (MarkStrideAlign.cpp:72-104); the fixpipe variant markAlignedDimForFixcctoub takes an explicit alignByte instead (:566-599).

Main traversal: runOnOperation gets a func::FuncOp, returns immediately for host functions (hacc::utils::isHost), reads archIsRegbased = isRegBasedArch(moduleOp) and archIs950 = isAscend950(moduleOp), then walks ops: non-HIVMStructuredOp ops are skipped; ops whose memref operands are all GM are skipped by noNeedAlign ('hasNonGMMemref' check); CustomOp/CustomMacroOp are handled from per-arg align_dim entries in their argAttrs dict; all other structured ops must satisfy hivmOp.hasPureBufferSemantics() or emitError 'Not bufferized.' and interrupt the walk (MarkStrideAlign.cpp:843-890, 826-841, 862-884).

Per-op skip conditions: VTransposeOp with isLastDimTranspose() is skipped ('already alloc size aligned, no need to do storage align'); on regbase VReduceOp with a reduce-with-index arith op is skipped ('f9 skips reduce-with-index on regbase; keep master's A2/A3 marking'); all-rank-0 memref types skipped; ops with no local-buffer (non-GM: UB/L1/L0C via isLocalBuffer) memref operand skipped; isUBDMAOp classifies hivm Load/Store/Copy (MarkStrideAlign.cpp:892-913; isLocalBuffer accepts UB|L1|L0C and rejects GM, Utils.cpp:462-476).

RegBase (A5) dim decision: all-ones shapes are skipped except FixpipeOp (comment: fixpipe may write through a subview/collapse producing <1x1> while the root alloc has non-unit dims); memref types are filtered to UB address space only (filterNonHivmSpace); because A5 hfusion-flatten has already merged axes, an identity reassociation is built and getLastDiscontinuousDimRegBased(filterMemrefTypes, identityReassoc, isUBDMAOp) decides the align dim (MarkStrideAlign.cpp:915-942); the A2/A3 branch instead requires FlattenInterface and uses getFlattened(checkMarkStride=true) + getLastDiscontinuousDim (:982-1009).

getLastDiscontinuousDimRegBased logic: if any memref has non-unit stride on the last dim, the last non-unit axis must be aligned (getLastNotUnitDim); else for UB DMA ops (copy_gm_to_ub / copy_ub_to_gm / copy_ub_to_ub) there is a shortcut: if every UB-space memref satisfies isSubLowDimStrideAlign && isNotTailJumpOrStrideAlign, no mark (nullopt); a 1-D memref yields nullopt; otherwise getLastNotUnitDim over the reassociation picks the dim (MarkStrideAlign.cpp:224-263); helpers: isNotTailJumpOrStrideAlign is true when the lowest-dim size equals the sub-low-dim stride or that stride is UB-align (e.g. memref<3x13xi8, strided<[16,1]>>) (:109-128); isSubLowDimStrideAlign requires rank>2 and the sub-low dim stride to be UB-align (:133-150).

Fixpipe special path (regbase): getLastDiscontinuousDimRegBasedForFixcctoub requires a 2-D L0C->UB fixpipe; N-size and M-size stride requirements come from hardcoded tables keyed by (data width, channel split, NZ2ND/NZ2DN dma mode, loop enhance, dual-dst mode) — e.g. {B16, DN_Y, N} -> 16 elements, {B8, ND_Y, N} -> 32, {B4, ND_Y, N} -> 64, {B32, DN_Y, N} -> 8; each requirement becomes alignBytes = stride * dataWidth / 8 attached to the trailing reassociation index (N) and second-to-last (M); DualDstMode comes from the fixpipe attr or the hivm.tiling_dim of a tightly-coupled-buffer mark; all UB target-space operands are marked via markAlignedDimForFixcctoub, and 3d-dot tiled fixpipes additionally mark the root alloc on dim 1 via adjustAlignInfo (MarkStrideAlign.cpp:601-699, 704-718, 721-824, 943-981).

Mark targeting and emission: ubOperands = hivmOp.getTargetSpaceOperands(AddressSpace::UB, /*includeTmpBuffer=*/false); for a hivm StoreOp with exactly one UB operand, the trailing-unit rank-reduced subview pattern (getTrailingUnitRankReducedSubviewInfo) may remap the align dim to result coordinates or retarget the mark to the subview's source (fixAlignDimForSingleUBStoreSubview); for each operand the pass skips when a hivm LoadOp's markTarget root carries PreMarkStrideAlign's skip_stride_align_for_vload annotation (shouldSkipStrideAlignForVLoad traces to root via traceToRoot), refines the dim with adjustAlignDim, then emits markAlignedDim; any walk interruption ends in signalPassFailure (MarkStrideAlign.cpp:517-524, 1011-1059, 1107-1113).

RegBase-only second walk over func::CallOp call arguments: skips operands already marked (isMarked checks users for annotation ops carrying stride_align_dims), all-rank-0 types, non-local-buffer types, and on Ascend950 any element width != 1 bit; computes reshape dims/permutations via getDimAxisInfo (VBrc/VReduce/VTranspose/VConcat/VPad/VGather), continuous reassociations, then the same getLastDiscontinuousDim + shouldSkipStrideAlignForVLoad + adjustAlignDim + markAlignedDim chain; after the arg loop, markForVsstb marks vf-call inputs to avoid vsstb bank conflicts (MarkStrideAlign.cpp:1061-1110). After the arg loop, markForVsstb walks each callee for vector::TransferWriteOp that isTransferWriteSuitForStoreWithStride, traces the source through subview/view to a func block argument, skips operands used by memref.collapse_shape/memref.reshape (in-code TODO: padding would create discontinuous shapes those users cannot handle), and marks the corresponding call operand at alignDim rank-2 with alignSizeForBankConflict — the comment 'Davinci recommends the vsstb stride align to (512*N + 32) Byte' realized as (16*N + 1) elements scaled by element byte width (kVsstbBankConflictAlignUnit=16, kVsstbSubTailDimOffset=2) (MarkStrideAlign.cpp:494-564).

Refinement gate adjustAlignDim (AdjustAlignUtil.cpp:517-549): returns nullopt when isNoNeedAlign; returns nullopt for ImplByScalarOpInterface ops that will lower to scalar loops ('no need to stride align because it will be decomposed to scalar operation later'); otherwise per-op adjustments — VBrc, VReduce, VDeinterleave, Copy special cases; hivm Load/Store with MayImplicitTransposeWithLastAxis return nullopt; inline-broadcastable ops go through adjustInlineBrcOp; everything else passes the dim through unchanged.

Pipeline placement (regbase): alignStoragePipeline (HIVMRegbasePipelines.cpp:484-494) adds AlignAllocSizePass (:487), then when hivmPipelineOptions.enableHIVMAutoStorageAlign nests PreMarkStrideAlignPass (:489) and MarkStrideAlignPass (:490) under func::FuncOp, then memref FoldAllocReshape (:492), then module-level EnableStrideAlignPass (:493); alignStoragePipeline is called at :560 inside hivmPostBufferizationOptimizationPipeline (:514-565, with decompose phases named BEFORE_HIVM_STRIDE_ALIGNMENT :542-543 and AFTER_HIVM_STRIDE_ALIGNMENT :561-563, followed by InferHIVMDataLayout :568); that pipeline is invoked at :699 inside buildLowerHIVMPipelines (:693-706) immediately after bufferizationPipeline (:695); registered as the 'lower-hivm-pipeline' pass pipeline (:712-719).

Gate option: def EnableHIVMAutoStorageAlign : HIVMOptimizationControlOptions<"Enable mark/enable storage align.", "bool", "true"> (Options.td:629-634) — the gate covers both the mark pass and the enable pass and defaults to on; the membase (A2/A3) alignStoragePipeline in HIVMPipelines.cpp:377-384 uses the same gate but adds only MarkStrideAlignPass (no PreMarkStrideAlign), and ConvertHIVMToStandard receives isOpsAligned = options.enableHIVMAutoStorageAlign (:539-543).

Consumer contract: EnableStrideAlign is def Pass<"hivm-enable-stride-align", "ModuleOp">, summary 'Align memref allocations according to stride align marks', description 'Re-allocate memrefs according to anntations of storage_align marks. ModuleOp scope is required so FuncOp-parallel nesting cannot race when aligned allocs propagate through func.call into VF callees' (Passes.td:888-900); its patterns read exactly the producer's mark — they require stride_align_dims and stride_align_value_in_byte on the annotation mark and fail with emitError when either is missing or their lengths differ (EnableStrideAlign.cpp:61-80); the pass normalizes/sorts mark info, propagates marks up to root allocations through view-like ops (cast/subview/collapse_shape/expand_shape/reshape/view per Util.h:36-42), down to leaf operands and among a hivm op's UB operands (union of align info, bounded at 10 iterations with an emitError at the cap), then EnableAlignAllocation re-creates allocs with padded static dims + a subview of the original shape and replaceAndPropagateMemRefType; regbase additionally runs materializeRemainingStaticUBLayoutCasts, and the hivm.storage_aligned func attr is set on membase only ('regbase (A5) targets must not carry this attribute') (EnableStrideAlign.cpp:131-161, 359-445, 536-634, 738-809).

Producer-side test corpus: the only test file that runs -hivm-mark-stride-align is hivm-mark-stride-align-fixcctoub.mlir (RUN: bishengir-opt %s -hivm-mark-stride-align -split-input-file | FileCheck %s -check-prefix=AIC, :1); its CHECK lines pin the printed mark form 'annotation.mark %alloc {hivm.stride_align_dims = array<i32: 1>, hivm.stride_align_value_in_byte = array<i32: 32>}' for Ascend950PR_9579 AIC fixpipe cases (:3-5 and 25 cases); test 24 covers the fixpipe all-ones exception (3x1x1 alloc through a 1x1 subview/collapse, :371-407) and test 25 is a negative case — with last-dim stride already 32 (memref<2x1x32xf32> strided<[32,1]>) the expected output is 'AIC-NOT: annotation.mark %alloc' (:411-434).

Consumer-side tests use hand-authored producer marks: bishenghivm-enable-stride-align-propagate-scope.mlir writes 'annotation.mark %alloc {hivm.stride_align_dims = array<i32: 1>, hivm.stride_align_value_in_byte = array<i32: 32>}' on a memref<2x15xf16, ub> alloc and expects -hivm-enable-stride-align to produce a padded memref<2x15x16xf16> alloc plus a subview of type strided<[240, 16]> flowing through scope.return (:7-21); enable-stride-align-rank-reducing-subview.mlir places the same mark shape on a rank-reducing subview result (:1-18) — i.e. the tests encode the same (dim, byte) mark contract MarkStrideAlign emits.

What 'stride align' aligns to: util::getHWAlignBytes(memorySpaceAttr) returns hivm::util::BL for AddressSpace UB and L1 and report_fatal_error otherwise (Utils.cpp:1413-1432); BL is defined as VL / 8 with VL = 256, i.e. 32 bytes (Utils.h:526-528) — so the default mark value is a 32-byte (256-bit vector block) stride alignment for on-chip buffers.

PreMarkStrideAlign (hivm-pre-mark-stride-align, func::FuncOp, Passes.td:860-874) is the sibling veto producer: its header states it detects 'DMA-loaded buffers that will be vload'd in vector functions where stride alignment would create inter-row gaps (non-contiguous layout) that vldsx1 (128-element consecutive flat-pointer load) cannot handle' and marks their root allocs for MarkStrideAlign to skip; runOnOperation returns early when not archIsRegbased, walks hivm::LoadOp results, follows users through view-like ops and casts to func.call sites whose callee reads that argument with vector::TransferReadOp, and annotates the alloc-like root with an annotation.mark carrying skip_stride_align_for_vload; MarkStrideAlign consults it via shouldSkipStrideAlignForVLoad in both of its walks (PreMarkStrideAlign.cpp:19-25, 58-64, 72-128, 139-188; MarkStrideAlign.cpp:1044-1049, 1093-1097).

"Marking stride-aligned buffers" is decision-recording, not transformation, and it must run post-bufferization: the pass changes no op, no type, and no layout — it only attaches (dimension, bytes) decisions as annotation marks, the physical padding (bigger alloc + strided subview) happens in EnableStrideAlign (EV-002, EV-004, EV-010 vs EV-016, EV-018); and its own legality makes the memref world unavoidable — tensor-typed operands and ops without pure buffer semantics are hard errors (EV-004, EV-005), while the decision inputs (strided layouts, UB address spaces, alloc shapes) only exist after bufferization. No single comment states either motivation end-to-end; this is an inference from those facts.

The reviewed test corpus exercises the mark pass's decision logic directly only for the fixpipe path (hivm-mark-stride-align-fixcctoub.mlir); no reviewed test runs -hivm-mark-stride-align over the generic structured-op path (load/store/elementwise on regbase) or the A2/A3 flatten path, so the exact marks chosen for those shapes on current HEAD were not observed — only their code paths were read.
records.note: recorded as absence of evidence, not as a claim that the paths are untested in the full suite
